column1: What does business agility enable an organization to do?
column2: Respond quickly to market changes and opportunities with innovative solutions.
column3: Business agility involves the whole organization, not only software teams.

column1: A competitor changes customer expectations. What response shows business agility?
column2: Learn what customers now need and adapt the solution quickly.
column3: A fast response requires coordination between business and technology.

column1: Why can functional silos slow value delivery?
column2: Work waits for handoffs and approvals between departments.
column3: Organizing people around value reduces unnecessary dependencies and delays.

column1: In SAFe, what is a value stream?
column2: The sequence of activities used to deliver value to a customer.
column3: A value stream crosses the functions needed to deliver an outcome.

column1: What is the difference between an operational value stream and a development value stream?
column2: An operational value stream delivers value to a customer. A development value stream builds and maintains solutions that support it.
column3: For example, processing an insurance claim is operational. Building the claim system is development.

column1: Why does SAFe use both a hierarchy and a network organized around value?
column2: The hierarchy supports stability and expertise. The network supports fast collaboration and response.
column3: The network connects people across functions without requiring the hierarchy to disappear.

column1: What is the purpose of organizing around value rather than individual functions?
column2: Reduce handoffs and deliver customer outcomes faster.
column3: People with different skills collaborate around a shared flow of work.

column1: How does a Lean-Agile organization respond to an untested product idea?
column2: Test the idea with customers and use the feedback to decide what to do next.
column3: Small experiments reduce the risk of investing heavily in an unwanted solution.

column1: Why is a software team's agility alone insufficient for business agility?
column2: Other parts of the organization must also support rapid decisions and value delivery.
column3: Slow funding or approval processes can block even a fast development team.

column1: What distinguishes a Lean-Agile transformation from adopting a few team ceremonies?
column2: It changes leadership, funding, organization, and ways of working to improve value delivery.
column3: Team practices help, but business agility also depends on the surrounding system.
